lanes.label: The seventy weeks and the last vision
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Daniel: overview
nodes.d: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, serve under Babylonian and Persian kings, and are delivered in the furnace and lions' den; Daniel interprets dreams and receives visions of kingdoms, the Ancient of days, and the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Daniel and his three friends and say how the book of Daniel is arranged?
ev: Name Daniel and his three friends with their Babylonian names (1:6-7)
Say which kings Daniel served (1:21, 5:31, 6:28)
Describe the two halves of the book: stories (1-6) and visions (7-12)

nodes.t: Daniel and his friends refuse the king's food
nodes.d: Taken to Babylon and chosen for training, Daniel determines not to defile himself with the king's food and wine; after a ten-day trial of vegetables and water they look healthier, and God gives the four young men knowledge and wisdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Daniel and his friends refused the king's food and what happened in Daniel 1?
ev: Retell why Daniel asked not to eat the king's food (1:8)
Describe the ten-day test (1:11-16)
Say what God gave the four young men (1:17)

nodes.t: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great image
nodes.d: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him his forgotten dream; Daniel and his friends seek God, who reveals the dream of an image of gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay struck by a stone that becomes a mountain, which Daniel interprets as kingdoms and God's kingdom that will never be destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the dream of the image and say what Daniel says the stone represents in Daniel 2:44-45?
ev: Describe the image and the stone (2:31-35)
Say what Daniel says of God in 2:20-22 and 2:28
Report Daniel's interpretation of the parts and the stone (2:37-45)

nodes.t: The fiery furnace
nodes.d: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image and orders everyone to worship it; Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse, are thrown into a blazing furnace, and are seen walking unharmed with a fourth figure, so the king praises their God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were thrown into the furnace and what happened in Daniel 3?
ev: Retell the king's command and the three men's answer (3:4-6, 16-18)
Describe what the king sees in the furnace (3:24-25)
Say how the king responds (3:28-30)

nodes.t: Nebuchadnezzar's tree and his humbling
nodes.d: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree cut down, Daniel interprets it as the king being driven from men until he knows the Most High rules, and the king, proud of Babylon, loses his reason for seven times and then praises the King of heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Nebuchadnezzar's great tree and say what he learned in Daniel 4:34-37?
ev: Describe the dream (4:10-17)
Say what Daniel advises the king (4:27)
Retell what happens to Nebuchadnezzar and how it ends (4:30-37)

nodes.t: The writing on the wall
nodes.d: At Belshazzar's feast, where the temple vessels are used to praise idols, fingers write on the wall; Daniel reads MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN as the numbering, weighing and dividing of the kingdom, and that night Belshazzar is slain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what appeared at Belshazzar's feast and what Daniel said it meant in Daniel 5?
ev: Describe the feast and the writing (5:1-5)
Say what Daniel reminds Belshazzar of (5:18-23)
Report the meaning of the writing and what happens (5:25-31)

nodes.t: Daniel in the lions' den
nodes.d: Under King Darius, officials who cannot find fault with Daniel secure a decree against prayer to anyone but the king; Daniel keeps praying to God toward Jerusalem, is thrown to the lions, and is found unharmed in the morning because God shut their mouths.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Daniel in the lions' den and say why he was thrown there in Daniel 6?
ev: Retell why the officials plot against Daniel (6:4-9)
Describe how Daniel prays and what happens (6:10-23)
Say what Darius decrees at the end (6:25-27)

nodes.t: Four beasts and the Ancient of days
nodes.d: In Belshazzar's first year Daniel dreams of four beasts rising from the sea, the last with ten horns and a boastful little horn; thrones are set, the Ancient of days sits in judgment, the beast is slain, and one like a son of man is given an everlasting kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the four beasts, the Ancient of days and the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:1-14?
ev: Describe the four beasts (7:3-8)
Describe the Ancient of days and the judgment (7:9-12)
Describe the one like the Son of man and what he is given (7:13-14)

nodes.t: The vision of the beasts interpreted
nodes.d: An attendant tells Daniel the four beasts are four kings, the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom for ever, and the little horn wars against the saints and speaks against the Most High until judgment is given and the kingdom is given to the saints.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Daniel is told the beasts are and what happens to the saints in Daniel 7:15-27?
ev: Say what the beasts and horns are told to be (7:17, 23-24)
Describe what the little horn does (7:21, 25)
Say what happens to the saints and the kingdom (7:18, 22, 26-27)

nodes.t: The ram, the goat and the little horn
nodes.d: In the third year of Belshazzar Daniel sees a two-horned ram defeated by a goat with a great horn, which is broken into four, and a little horn that attacks the sanctuary and the daily sacrifice; Gabriel explains the ram as Media and Persia and the goat as Greece.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the ram and the goat in Daniel 8 and what Gabriel says they are?
ev: Describe the ram, goat and horns (8:3-12)
Report what Gabriel says the ram and goat are (8:20-21)
Say what length of time is given until the sanctuary is cleansed (8:13-14) and how Daniel responds (8:27)

nodes.t: Daniel's prayer of confession
nodes.d: Reading in Jeremiah that Jerusalem's desolation would last seventy years, Daniel prays with fasting, confessing that Israel has sinned and not heeded the prophets, that the curse written in the law of Moses has come, and asks God to act for his own name's sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what prompted Daniel's prayer in Daniel 9:2 and what he confesses?
ev: Say what Daniel understood from the books (9:2)
List elements of his confession (9:5-14)
Say on what ground he asks God to hear (9:16-19)

nodes.t: Gabriel and the seventy weeks
nodes.d: While Daniel prays, Gabriel comes to give him understanding: seventy weeks are determined for his people and the holy city to finish transgression and bring in everlasting righteousness, with the Messiah the Prince, a city rebuilt, a Messiah cut off, and a desolation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel says the seventy weeks are for in Daniel 9:24?
ev: Say when Gabriel comes and why (9:20-23)
List what the seventy weeks are for (9:24)
Report what is said of the Messiah the Prince and of the city and the sanctuary (9:25-27)

nodes.t: A vision of a man clothed in linen
nodes.d: In the third year of Cyrus Daniel mourns three weeks and, by the river Hiddekel, sees a man in linen with a radiant appearance whose voice leaves him without strength; he is strengthened, told his words were heard, and that a struggle with the prince of Persia involved Michael.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Daniel saw by the river Hiddekel and how he was strengthened in Daniel 10?
ev: Describe the man Daniel sees (10:5-6)
Say how Daniel responds and is strengthened (10:7-19)
Say what the messenger says of the prince of Persia and Michael (10:12-13, 20-21)

nodes.t: Kings of the south and the north
nodes.d: The messenger tells Daniel of Persian kings, a mighty king whose kingdom is divided to the four winds, and a long series of conflicts between kings of the south and north including alliance by marriage, wars and a raiser of taxes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the pattern of conflict between the kings of the south and north in Daniel 11:5-20?
ev: Say what is said of the mighty king and his kingdom (11:3-4)
Describe the rivalry between the king of the south and the king of the north (11:5-20)

nodes.t: The contemptible king and the time of the end
nodes.d: A vile person gains a kingdom by flatteries, turns against the holy covenant, takes away the daily sacrifice and sets up the abomination of desolation; the wise instruct many and some fall; a king exalts himself above every god until his end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Daniel 11:31-35 says happens to the sanctuary and to the people who know their God?
ev: Describe how the vile person rises (11:21-24)
Say what he does to the sanctuary and the covenant (11:28-32)
Say what happens to the people who know their God (11:32-35) and to the king in 11:36-45

nodes.t: Michael stands up; many shall awake
nodes.d: Michael stands up in a time of trouble, those written in the book are delivered, many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, the wise shine like stars, and Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end and go his way to rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Daniel 12:2-3 says will happen to those who sleep in the dust and to the wise?
ev: Quote the promise in Daniel 12:2-3
Say what Daniel is told to do with the book (12:4, 9)
Report what Daniel is told for himself (12:13)

nodes.t: Seventy years and the cup of wrath
nodes.d: In Jehoiakim's fourth year Jeremiah reminds Judah of twenty-three years of unheeded warnings; Babylon will rule seventy years and then be punished, and the nations are made to drink the cup of the LORD's fury.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah 25:11-12 says about seventy years and what happens to Babylon afterward?
ev: Say how long Jeremiah had spoken (25:3)
Say what the LORD says about the seventy years (25:11-12)
Describe the cup the nations drink (25:15-29)

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: The abomination of desolation and the great tribulation
nodes.d: Jesus tells those in Judaea to flee when they see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel, describes great tribulation and warns against false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told his disciples to do when they see the abomination of desolation?
ev: Say what Jesus tells those in Judaea to do
Explain the warning about false Christs

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: The Olivet discourse: signs and the abomination
nodes.d: Leaving the temple, Jesus foretells the buildings’ destruction and on the Mount of Olives warns of deceivers, wars, persecution and the gospel preached to all nations; he warns of the abomination of desolation, great affliction and false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus said to watch for?
ev: State the disciples’ question (13:4)
List the warnings Jesus gave

nodes.t: Revelation: overview
nodes.d: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?
ev: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3

nodes.t: John's vision of Christ among the lampstands
nodes.d: John on Patmos hears a voice and sees one like the Son of man among seven golden candlesticks, with eyes like fire and a two-edged sword from his mouth, who says he is first and last, alive for evermore, holding the keys of death and hell.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vision of Christ in Revelation 1 and what he says to John?
ev: Describe what John saw
Say what Christ says about himself in 1:17-18
Say what the seven stars and seven candlesticks are in 1:20

nodes.t: The throne in heaven
nodes.d: John is called up through an open door and sees a throne with one sitting on it, a rainbow, twenty-four elders in white with crowns, four living creatures crying holy, holy, holy, and all worship God as Creator.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the throne room scene and what the worshippers say?
ev: Describe what surrounds the throne
Say what the four beasts and the elders say and do
Say why God is worthy according to 4:11

nodes.t: The woman, the dragon and the man child
nodes.d: John sees a woman clothed with the sun who bears a man child who is caught up to God, a great red dragon who tries to devour the child, war in heaven in which the dragon is cast down, and the dragon's pursuit of the woman and her seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the main figures of Revelation 12 and what the text says each does?
ev: Describe the woman, the dragon and the child
Say who the dragon is named in 12:9
Say how the saints overcome him in 12:11
Describe what the dragon does after he is cast down

nodes.t: The beast from the sea and the beast from the earth
nodes.d: John sees a beast rise out of the sea receiving authority from the dragon and making war on the saints, and a second beast from the earth that makes people worship the first, speaks as a dragon, and imposes a mark and the number 666.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe both beasts in Revelation 13 and what they cause people to do?
ev: Describe the first beast and what it is given
Describe what the second beast does
Say whose names are not written in the book of life in 13:8

nodes.t: Satan loosed, the great white throne and the lake of fire
nodes.d: After the thousand years Satan is loosed and gathers Gog and Magog, fire from God devours them, the devil is cast into the lake of fire, and the dead are judged before a great white throne by their works, with death and hell cast into the lake of fire and those not in the book of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the great white throne judgment as Revelation 20:11-15 shows it?
ev: Describe what Satan does when loosed and what happens to him
Say what is judged and by what in 20:12-13
Say what is cast into the lake of fire in 20:14-15
